applypy_command: apply.py --pre-stage CMD (between decode and vfx) and --post-stage CMD (between vfx and encode), repeatable, run in the order given; CMD is one command line split without a shell; {width} {height} {depth} {fps} (N/D) {frames} {pix_fmt} are filled in; --stage-timeout S (default 120, 0 off). The stage reads whole frames of the --depth format on stdin and writes the same number of frames of the same size and format on stdout; frames/1 error codes; every hop between two processes is relayed by a thread of apply.py in chunks of 1 MiB
neutral_ffmpeg_recipe: a neutral-handoff binary that reads frames from stdin, runs a FrameStage and writes frames to stdout would be this slot; the pipeline crate that spawns vfx itself is the alternative
difference_or_hazard: {frames} is refused when the count is unknown (variable rate input); a stage that writes fewer frames is broken_pipe, half a frame is partial_frame, a stage that writes more frames is not named (the run ends with 'the output did not verify: duration is ...'); a stage that is silent for the timeout while computing is killed (R32)
